answer: Current uninstall on this Linux worktree is two measured surfaces, never operator HOME/crontab/systemd. (1) astplugin CLI (platform/plugin/astplugin.py uninstall --retain-user-data) against a throwaway prefix: it deletes provenance-tracked live files ['commands/astplugin.md', 'hooks/plugin_health.py'] and version dirs; userdata and unrelated host-profile hooks.json/.mcp.json/scheduled-tasks survive; the deployed hook file hooks/plugin_health.py is gone after uninstall (present after install=True). astplugin does not register Claude-style hook/MCP/scheduled-task ids, so those cannot orphan from this CLI. Prefix residuals vs pre-install: ['dir:live/commands', 'dir:live/hooks', 'dir:state/staging', 'state/journal.jsonl'] (journal + empty deploy-target dirs; documented, not user-data). (2) Host-profile registration driver in probes/TST-0073: complete uninstall leaves zero package hook/MCP/scheduled-task ids; pre/post census has one documented-intentional residual (user-data/install-created-session.json). Payload-only delete leaves 4 dangling registrations and the host still activates them. Scorched-earth clears orphans but destroys user data, so a zero-orphan claim without the survival census is not evidence.

negative_controls.description: Delete only package/ and leave registrations. The orphan sweep must report leftover hook/MCP/task and the host must still activate them. Complete uninstall on a sibling profile must report zero orphans, or the detector is vacuous.
Delete the entire profile. Orphan count is zero (the sweep would pass) but documented user data is gone. The survival census must fail, proving zero-orphan is not sufficient.
